# kind mu_squared momenta... squared_mass_real_imag... finite_real_imag pole1_real_imag pole2_real_imag
# One-mass D0 (OneLOop's boxf1, m1 = m2 = m3 = 0) with a complex mass, where OneLOop 3.6 is
# wrong in double and quadruple precision alike, and so was this crate before it took Denner
# and Dittmaier's sheets for a width (box_integral::one_mass_complex_sheets). OneLOop's value
# is in the comment before each row. The first rows are NinjaRS's reproducer
# 4 1.0 P 14.78 12.26 -18.32 15.39 -17.48 0 0 0 0 0 0 3.018 -0.302: OneLOop (and this crate
# before) jumps between P = -0.06 (right, -0.0250 - 3.2e-4i) and P = -0.05 to 0.0254 + 1.87i;
# the integral is analytic in P < 0. Then its second reproducer, then 10 of the 131 rows of a
# sweep of 3000 random one-mass boxes (widths 1e-3 to 0.5 of the mass, 30% with an invariant
# between massless lines of 1e-10 to 1e-2) that OneLOop and this crate got wrong (by 0.3 to 7
# relative to the value), in the same rows.
# References: Denner and Dittmaier's one-mass box (arXiv:1005.2076, eqs. (3.82)-(3.83): the
# continued dilogarithms with eta terms of the principal logarithms of x_k and of the ratios
# Y23/Y02, Y03/m^2, Y13/Y01), in mpmath at 40 digits with the exact binary64 inputs. COLLIER
# 1.2.9 in quadruple precision (its COLI and DD branches, independent of both OneLOop and this
# crate) agrees within the bound in the comment. A direct Feynman-parameter integral
# (primary sectors, contour deformation x -> x - i lambda x (1 - x) dRe F/dx, nested tanh-sinh
# in numpy, no closed-form one-loop code; lambda = 0.1 and 0.15 agree) gives at P = -1e-3
# -0.038009941931 - 5.0219345e-4i (2e-11 from the reference; OneLOop 0.321 + 13.18i) and at
# P = -1e-6 -0.0599040232 - 8.18212e-4i (1e-9; OneLOop 6.11 + 383i). It does not converge
# for the second reproducer (D0 = -1219 + 77i for the real mass); along its width from 0 to
# -0.49 OneLOop agrees with COLLIER up to 1e-4, not at 1e-2 to 0.2, again at 0.3, and not
# at 0.4 and 0.49, while these expressions agree everywhere.
